compiled_state.title: As a DSO maintainer, a new code-reviewer-verifier agent evaluates absence-claim findings and emits structured rulings with fingerprints
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Description

**What**: Build a new `code-reviewer-verifier` sub-agent that inspects critical/important/fragile findings at the cited file (via snapshot SHA) and emits one of three rulings: confirm / downgrade-to-minor / drop.

**Why**: Invalid absence-claim findings currently reach the autonomous-resolution loop unchanged. The verifier pre-surfaces them and filters or downgrades invalid ones before they consume resolution attempts.

**Scope**:
- IN: `plugins/dso/agents/code-reviewer-verifier.md` creation; ruling schema; fingerprint schema (including multi-file and non-line-anchored sentinels); rubric (defer to reviewer on uncertainty, never drop on insufficient evidence); per-finding failure handling (`verifier_status: failed`, fail-open); ruling semantics (confirm enters loop unchanged; downgrade-to-minor becomes minor PR comment; drop removes finding)
- OUT: Dispatch wiring into CI or local paths (S4, S5), feature flag (S6), telemetry emission (S6)

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, `plugins/dso/agents/code-reviewer-verifier.md` exists with ruling shape: `{finding_id, ruling: confirm|downgrade-to-minor|drop, fingerprint: "<path>:<line-start>-<line-end>", verifier_status: ok|failed, evidence_invalidated: bool, rationale}`; schema validates the output at the verifier boundary
  ← Satisfies: "code-reviewer-verifier sub-agent file exists at plugins/dso/agents/code-reviewer-verifier.md"
- When this story is complete, rubric is: defer to reviewer on uncertainty (verifier never drops a finding on insufficient evidence — confirms and lets the existing autonomous-resolution loop handle it); drops only when finding is verifiably false; downgrades when claim is true but reachability, scope, or severity is wrong
  ← Satisfies: "Verifier rulings have explicit semantics in the autonomous-resolution loop"
- When this story is complete, fingerprint schema specifies behavior for: (a) findings spanning multiple files (one fingerprint per file); (b) findings without a line anchor (e.g., missing-file claims — fingerprint is `<path>:0-0` sentinel); (c) findings on deleted files (`<path>:0-0` sentinel); schema validator rejects malformed fingerprints with a clear error; `line-start == line-end` constraint enforced on single-line findings
  ← Satisfies: "Per-ruling file:line-region fingerprint emitted for every verified finding; shape <path>:<line-start>-<line-end> with line-start == line-end on single-line findings; validated by schema"
- When this story is complete, any verifier failure (timeout, malformed output, API error) annotates the finding with `verifier_status: failed` and passes it through unchanged (fail-open per finding)
  ← Satisfies: "Verifier failure handling: any failure annotates the finding with verifier_status: failed and passes it through unchanged"
- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic

## Considerations

- [Testing] Verifier LLM rubric correctness is probabilistic — behavioral fixtures from brainstorm probes (Test 1: clear contradiction drop 3/3; Test 2: authoritative tone drop 3/3; Test 3: genuine ambiguity defer) anchor behavior but don't guarantee runtime accuracy

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
